newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Rebel leader gives Zaire's Mobutu ultimatum.
newsitem.headline: Rebel leader gives Zaire's Mobutu ultimatum.

text.p: Zairean rebel leader Laurent Kabila on Wednesday gave President Mobutu Sese Seko until February 21 to surrender power or face a major rebel attack.
"Unless Mobutu can come to the table and agree to relinquish power we shall have no choice but to launch a major offensive," he told Reuters in the rebel-held city of Goma.
Kabila also accused France and Belgium of recruiting 300 foreign mercenaries. He said seven of the mercenaries had already been killed in clashes with his forces.
"France and Belgiyum are recruiting and paying for the mercenaries but they will be defeated because the population is on our side," he said.
The Zairean government admits it has hired foreign mercenaries, many of whom are from former Yugoslavia, but France and Belgium deny they are the paymasters.
The Tutsi-led rebels launched their campaign in October, accusing the Zairean authorities of denying them citizenship and seeking to return them to Rwanda, which their forebears left generations ago.
The army began a counter-offensive on January 20, but it has failed to dislodge the rebels from towns and territory along the borders with Rwanda, Uganda and Burundi.

In their most recent success this week, the rebels have captured the strategic transport hub of Kalemie on Lake Tanganyika. Kalemie, with its port and airport, has links to the whole mineral-producing province of Shaba.
Kabila said his forces were now advancing on Moba, about 150 km (90 miles) south of Kalemie. He said they were about 40 km (25 miles) from the town.
